format:

    margin:
      top: 2.1cm

      right: 1.7cm
    mainfont: "Segoe UI"
    section-numbering: ""
brand:
  color:
    palette:
      paper: "#FFFFFF"
      ink: "#22282E"
      ink-soft: "#5C666F"
      red: "#C10016"
      blue: "#0F4C81"
    background: paper
    foreground: ink
    primary: blue

  # No font is named beyond the one above, so nothing is fetched from a font
  # service; a system without it falls back to the default of the renderer.
  typography:
    headings:
      weight: bold
      color: red
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    echo: false
    message: false
    warning: false
    dev: "ragg_png"
    dev.args: {bg: "white"}
    dpi: 300
    fig-width: 6.8
    fig-height: 2.5
execute:
  error: true
---

```{r setup}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What to set for a report
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The path to the config file, whose esef section names the Silver layer of
# the module. A chunk runs with the directory of this template as its working
# directory, which is inside the installed package, so the path is taken from
# the environment variable FINCOMMONS_CONFIG where it is set and is otherwise
# a paths.yaml beside the template.
config_path <- Sys.getenv("FINCOMMONS_CONFIG", "paths.yaml")

# The countries the report covers, as the repository codes them, or NULL for
# every country the lake holds.
report_countries <- NULL

# The financial years shown, by the calendar year the period ends in, or
# NULL for the last `n_years` the lake holds. A financial year to 31 March
# 2026 counts as 2026 here, and is labelled 2025/26 wherever it is named.
report_years <- NULL
n_years <- 5

# How many rows the rankings of filings show.
top_n <- 15

# The point size of the text in a chart.
chart_base_size <- 9

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What each check is asked of
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The catalogue of checks says what a code means; it does not say which
# filings the check could have fired on, and a share is only readable
# against the right denominator. A check that reads the figures of a report
# can only fire on a filing the repository published facts for, and a filing
# listed without facts is not a filing that passed those checks.
#
#   "listed" -- every filing in the index, facts or not.
#   "read"   -- the filings the table of facts holds facts for, which is
#               what the pipeline has collected and not what the repository
#               could have given it.
#
# Every code of the catalogue has to appear here, or the report stops: a
# check added to the module and not to this list would otherwise be counted
# against whichever denominator happened to be lying around.
populations <- tibble::tribble(
  ~code,                   ~population,
  "IMBAL_BALANCE_SHEET",   "read",
  "IMBAL_ASSETS",          "read",
  "IMBAL_INCOME",          "read",
  "IMBAL_PROFIT",          "read",
  "IMBAL_CASHFLOW",        "read",
  "IMPL_NEGATIVE_ASSETS",  "read",
  "IMPL_PERIOD",           "read",
  "MISS_FACT_VALUE",       "read",
  "MISS_ASSETS",           "read",
  "MISS_REVENUE",          "read",
  "MISS_PROFIT",           "read",
  "DUPL_FACT_VALUE",       "read",
  "MIXED_UNIT",            "read",
  "IMPL_PRDEND_FUTURE",    "read",
  "DUPL_FILING_PERIOD",    "read",
  "HIGH_EXTENSION_SHARE",  "read",
  "VALIDATION_ERRORS",     "listed",
  "NO_FACTS",              "listed")

# The order the severities are read in, from the one that stops an analysis
# to the one that only describes it.
severities <- c("error", "warning", "info")

# What a row of the table of issues is about, which is what makes the two
# counts of this report different things. A check names the records that
# failed it: a filing, where the fault is a fault of the report as a whole,
# and a fact, where one figure of it is at fault. So a code that names facts
# has as many rows for one filing as that filing has bad facts.
#
#   findings -- rows of the table of issues.
#   affected -- distinct filings named by those rows.
#
# No table in this report adds a count of findings to a count of filings.

# You can adapt your corporate design in the sourced R-Skript. It is one file
# for the whole package, in the templates directory beside the modules, so
# that a report of either regime looks like the other and a change to the
# design is made once rather than once per module. A copy beside this
# template wins over it, which is what lets a template taken out of the
# package carry a design of its own.
library(ggplot2)
design_file <- "r-corporate-design-functions-ggplot2.R"
design_path <- c(design_file, file.path("..", "..", "templates", design_file))
design_path <- design_path[file.exists(design_path)]
if (length(design_path) == 0) {
  stop("The corporate design script ", design_file, " is neither beside this ",
       "template nor in the templates directory of the package.")
}
source(design_path[1])

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(yaml)
library(arrow)

# The label of a financial year. A year that ends on 31 December is named by
# its calendar year, and any other by the two it spans: a financial year to
# 31 March 2026 is 2025/26.
fy_label <- function(date) {
  y <- as.integer(format(date, "%Y"))
  ifelse(format(date, "%m-%d") == "12-31", as.character(y),
         paste0(y - 1, "/", sprintf("%02d", y %% 100)))
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The catalogue of checks
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The same file the module reads, so that the report describes the checks
# that ran rather than a copy of their descriptions that has drifted. It
# lives in the data directory of the package; a copy beside this template
# wins over it, as the design script does.
catalogue_file <- "dataquality_checks.csv"
catalogue_path <- c(catalogue_file,
                    file.path("..", "..", "data", catalogue_file))
catalogue_path <- catalogue_path[file.exists(catalogue_path)]
if (length(catalogue_path) == 0) {
  stop("The catalogue of checks ", catalogue_file, " is neither beside this ",
       "template nor in the data directory of the package.")
}

catalogue <- read.csv(catalogue_path[1], stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  filter(dataset == "esef") %>%
  as_tibble()

if (nrow(catalogue) == 0) {
  stop("The catalogue of checks names no check of the esef module.")
}

undeclared <- setdiff(catalogue$code, populations$code)
if (length(undeclared) > 0) {
  stop("The catalogue names checks this template does not know the ",
       "population of: ", paste(undeclared, collapse = ", "),
       ". Add them to `populations` in the settings of this template.")
}

unknown_severity <- setdiff(catalogue$severity, severities)
if (length(unknown_severity) > 0) {
  stop("The catalogue uses severities this template does not order: ",
       paste(unknown_severity, collapse = ", "), ".")
}

catalogue <- catalogue %>%
  left_join(populations, by = "code") %>%
  mutate(severity = factor(severity, levels = severities)) %>%
  arrange(severity, code)

n_checks <- nrow(catalogue)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The Silver layer
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

yaml_paths <- read_yaml(config_path)
path_silver <- yaml_paths[["esef"]][["silver"]]

# The Silver layer may name a schema in a catalogue rather than a directory,
# with the directory the tables are written to beside it. R reads files, so
# it takes the directory.
if (is.list(path_silver)) path_silver <- path_silver[["path"]]

# arrow reads every parquet file under a directory. A Delta table keeps the
# files it has replaced until it is vacuumed, and both of these tables are
# written a partition at a time, so a Delta table read this way counts a row
# once for every time it was written. This report counts rows, so it refuses
# one rather than show those counts.
for (table in c("filings", "facts", "issues")) {
  if (dir.exists(file.path(path_silver, table, "_delta_log"))) {
    stop("The ", table, " table of the esef module is a Delta table, which ",
         "this template does not read. Write the Silver layer as parquet, ",
         "or read the table through Spark.")
  }
}

if (!dir.exists(file.path(path_silver, "issues"))) {
  stop("The esef module has no table of issues in ", path_silver, ". Run the ",
       "checks first: python -c \"from pyspark.sql import SparkSession; ",
       "from fincommons.esef.quality import update_silver_esef_quality; ",
       "update_silver_esef_quality(SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate(), ",
       "'<paths.yaml>')\"")
}

filings_all <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "filings")) %>%
  select(COUNTRY, LEI, FILING, NAME, PERIODEND, LANG, JSONURL,
         ERRORS, WARNINGS, INCONSISTENCIES, PROCESSED) %>%
  collect()

if (nrow(filings_all) == 0) {
  stop("The table of filings of the esef module is empty. Run the pipeline ",
       "first: python -m fincommons.esef --config <paths.yaml> --country AT ",
       "--contact <you@example.org>")
}

# Which filings the table of facts holds facts for. A filing the repository
# published xBRL-JSON for is a filing the pipeline *could* have collected;
# only the table of facts says which it did, and a check that reads a figure
# could only have fired on those. One row per filing and not the facts
# themselves: arrow answers this over the parquet files and hands back a
# result of the size of the record rather than of the size of the lake.
facts_filings <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "facts")) %>%
  count(COUNTRY, LEI, FILING) %>%
  collect() %>%
  rename(facts = n)

issues_all <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "issues")) %>% collect()

if (nrow(issues_all) == 0) {
  stop("The table of issues of the esef module is empty. Either the checks ",
       "have not run over any country yet, or the Silver layer holds no ",
       "filing at all.")
}

# The partition column comes from the directory name when the table is
# written partitioned and from the file when it is not, and arrow reads the
# two as different types. One type here, so the joins below hold either way.
issues_all <- issues_all %>%
  mutate(across(c(COUNTRY, LEI, FILING, ISSUE), as.character),
         CHECKED = as.Date(CHECKED))

# A code in the table that the catalogue does not describe is a check that
# was removed or renamed and whose rows were left behind. The report cannot
# say what it means, so it stops rather than print a bare code.
uncatalogued <- setdiff(unique(issues_all$ISSUE), catalogue$code)
if (length(uncatalogued) > 0) {
  stop("The table of issues holds codes the catalogue does not describe: ",
       paste(uncatalogued, collapse = ", "), ". Run the checks again, which ",
       "rewrites the partitions it checks as a whole.")
}

filings_all <- filings_all %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(format(PERIODEND, "%Y")),
         fy = year,
         fy_name = fy_label(PERIODEND),
         published = !is.na(JSONURL) & JSONURL != "") %>%
  left_join(facts_filings %>% select(COUNTRY, LEI, FILING, facts),
            by = c("COUNTRY", "LEI", "FILING")) %>%
  mutate(read = !is.na(facts) & facts > 0,
         facts = coalesce(facts, 0L))

# The countries and the years the report covers. A country named in the
# settings that the table does not list is an error rather than an empty
# column, because a report that silently covers less than it says is worse
# than one that does not render.
countries_held <- sort(unique(filings_all$COUNTRY))
if (is.null(report_countries)) {
  report_countries <- countries_held
} else {
  unknown <- setdiff(report_countries, countries_held)
  if (length(unknown) > 0) {
    stop("The table of filings lists no filing of ",
         paste(unknown, collapse = ", "), ". It lists ",
         paste(countries_held, collapse = ", "), ".")
  }
}

years_held <- sort(unique(filings_all$fy[!is.na(filings_all$fy)]))
if (is.null(report_years)) {
  report_years <- tail(years_held, n_years)
} else {
  unknown <- setdiff(report_years, years_held)
  if (length(unknown) > 0) {
    stop("The table of filings lists no filing for ",
         paste(unknown, collapse = ", "), ".")
  }
}
report_years <- sort(report_years)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The record the checks were asked about
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Every filing of the selection, not one per issuer and year. A quality
# report counts what was checked, and a second filing of a year was checked
# like the first; the coverage report in this directory is the one that
# picks a filing per issuer and year.
filings <- filings_all %>%
  filter(COUNTRY %in% report_countries, fy %in% report_years)

if (nrow(filings) == 0) {
  stop("No filing of the table falls in the countries and years of this ",
       "report.")
}

year_labels <- filings %>%
  distinct(fy, fy_name) %>%
  arrange(fy) %>%
  group_by(fy) %>%
  summarise(label = paste(sort(unique(fy_name)), collapse = ", "),
            .groups = "drop")
year_labels <- vapply(report_years, function(y) {
  hit <- year_labels$label[year_labels$fy == y]
  if (length(hit) == 1 && !grepl(",", hit)) hit else as.character(y)
}, character(1))

# A partition of the table of filings with no row in the table of issues is
# either a partition every check passed or a partition no check has run
# over. Nothing in the two tables tells the two apart, so the report names
# the countries it cannot speak for rather than count them as sound.
checked_countries <- sort(unique(issues_all$COUNTRY))
silent_countries <- setdiff(report_countries, checked_countries)

issues <- issues_all %>%
  inner_join(filings %>% select(COUNTRY, LEI, FILING, NAME, fy, PERIODEND,
                                read),
             by = c("COUNTRY", "LEI", "FILING")) %>%
  left_join(catalogue %>% select(ISSUE = code, severity, title, population),
            by = "ISSUE")

# An issue row whose filing the table of filings does not list is a row left
# over from a filing the repository withdrew. It cannot be placed in a year
# or a country, so it is counted and set aside.
orphans <- issues_all %>%
  anti_join(filings_all %>% select(COUNTRY, LEI, FILING),
            by = c("COUNTRY", "LEI", "FILING"))

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What the checks found
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The two populations, and which of them the rates of this report are
# taken over.
#
# A check asked of every filing was also asked of every filing with facts,
# the one population being inside the other, so the filings with facts are
# the only population every check of the module was asked about. The rates
# of this report -- the share free of errors, the shares by year and by
# country, the bands of findings per filing -- are therefore taken over
# those, and a filing listed without facts is counted only in the two
# checks that read the index. Taken over the whole index instead, a record
# of which a thousandth has been collected would read as sound because
# nothing had looked at the rest of it.
n_listed <- nrow(filings)
n_read <- sum(filings$read)

# One row per code: the rows it wrote, the filings those rows name, and that
# count against the filings the check could have fired on at all.
by_code <- issues %>%
  group_by(ISSUE) %>%
  summarise(findings = n(),
            affected = n_distinct(FILING),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  right_join(catalogue %>% select(ISSUE = code, severity, title, population),
             by = "ISSUE") %>%
  mutate(findings = coalesce(findings, 0L),
         affected = coalesce(affected, 0L),
         denominator = ifelse(population == "listed", n_listed, n_read),
         share = ifelse(denominator > 0, affected / denominator * 100,
                        NA_real_)) %>%
  arrange(severity, desc(affected), ISSUE)

# One row per filing the checks named, with the severity of the worst thing
# found in it. A filing with no row here is one every check passed -- which,
# for a country no check has run over, is a statement this report does not
# make.
per_filing <- issues %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, LEI, FILING, NAME, fy, PERIODEND) %>%
  summarise(findings = n(),
            codes = n_distinct(ISSUE),
            errors = sum(severity == "error"),
            warnings = sum(severity == "warning"),
            infos = sum(severity == "info"),
            worst = severities[min(as.integer(severity))],
            which = paste(sort(unique(ISSUE)), collapse = ", "),
            .groups = "drop")

# Every filing of the selection, with a zero where no check named it.
filing_state <- filings %>%
  select(COUNTRY, LEI, FILING, NAME, fy, PERIODEND, read, facts) %>%
  left_join(per_filing %>% select(COUNTRY, LEI, FILING, findings, codes,
                                  errors, warnings, infos, worst, which),
            by = c("COUNTRY", "LEI", "FILING")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(findings, codes, errors, warnings, infos),
                ~ coalesce(.x, 0L)),
         worst = coalesce(worst, "none"),
         which = coalesce(which, ""),
         clean = errors == 0,
         spotless = findings == 0)

# The filings every check was asked of, which is what every rate below is
# taken over.
rated <- filing_state %>% filter(read)

if (nrow(rated) == 0) {
  stop("The table of facts holds no fact for any filing of this selection, ",
       "so no check that reads a figure could have run. Collect the reports ",
       "first: python -m fincommons.esef --config <paths.yaml> --country AT ",
       "--contact <you@example.org>")
}

# Per year: the record checked, and how much of the part of it with facts
# carries an error or carries nothing at all.
by_year <- filing_state %>%
  group_by(fy) %>%
  summarise(listed = n(),
            read = sum(read),
            findings = sum(findings),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(rated %>%
              group_by(fy) %>%
              summarise(with_error = sum(errors > 0),
                        clean = sum(clean) / n() * 100,
                        spotless = sum(spotless) / n() * 100,
                        error_share = sum(errors > 0) / n() * 100,
                        warning_share = sum(warnings > 0) / n() * 100,
                        info_share = sum(infos > 0) / n() * 100,
                        .groups = "drop"),
            by = "fy")

by_country <- filing_state %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY) %>%
  summarise(listed = n(),
            read = sum(read),
            findings = sum(findings),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(rated %>%
              group_by(COUNTRY) %>%
              summarise(with_error = sum(errors > 0),
                        error_share = sum(errors > 0) / n() * 100,
                        clean = sum(clean) / n() * 100,
                        per_filing = sum(findings) / n(),
                        .groups = "drop"),
            by = "COUNTRY") %>%
  arrange(desc(error_share), COUNTRY)

# The five identities, which are the checks that say the figures of a report
# are consistent with one another. They are grouped because an analysis that
# reads a statement out of a filing rests on all five at once.
identity_codes <- catalogue$code[grepl("^IMBAL_", catalogue$code)]
identity_state <- rated %>%
  left_join(issues %>%
              filter(ISSUE %in% identity_codes) %>%
              distinct(COUNTRY, LEI, FILING) %>%
              mutate(fails_identity = TRUE),
            by = c("COUNTRY", "LEI", "FILING")) %>%
  mutate(fails_identity = coalesce(fails_identity, FALSE))

checked_on <- range(issues_all$CHECKED)
```

```{r formats}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Writing numbers and words
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  x <- ifelse(!is.na(x) & abs(x) < 0.5 / 10^digits, 0, x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "–",
         formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",",
                 decimal.mark = "."))
}

wrap_caption <- function(text, width = 125) {
  paste(strwrap(text, width = width), collapse = "\n")
}

max_date <- max(filings$PERIODEND, na.rm = TRUE)
period_range <- paste0(min(report_years), " – ", max(report_years))

source_caption <- caption_corporate_design(
  source = paste("ESEF annual financial reports, filings.xbrl.org;",
                 "checks of the fincommons esef module."),
  last = format(max(checked_on), "%d %b %Y"),
  lang = "en")

typst_string <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("\\\\", "\\\\\\\\", x)
  gsub("\"", "\\\\\"", x)
}

severity_label <- function(x) {
  recode(as.character(x), error = "Error", warning = "Warning",
         info = "Note", none = "Nothing found")
}

# A table of one row per item and one column per financial year.
render_years <- function(data, value, digits = 0, label_column = "label",
                         header = "", order = NULL) {
  wide <- data %>%
    mutate(.v = {{ value }}) %>%
    select(all_of(label_column), fy, .v) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = "fy", values_from = ".v")
  if (!is.null(order)) {
    wide <- wide[match(order, wide[[label_column]]), ]
    wide[[label_column]] <- order
  }
  out <- tibble(item = wide[[label_column]])
  for (y in report_years) {
    column <- as.character(y)
    out[[column]] <- if (column %in% names(wide)) fmt(wide[[column]], digits)
                     else "–"
  }
  knitr::kable(out, col.names = c(header, year_labels),
               align = paste0("l", strrep("r", length(report_years))))
}

# A chart of one line per group over the financial years.
chart_by_year <- function(data, value, group, subtitle = "%", digits = 0,
                          ncol = 5, zero = TRUE) {
  d <- data %>% mutate(.v = {{ value }}, .g = {{ group }}) %>% filter(!is.na(.v))
  g <- ggplot(d, aes(x = fy, y = .v, colour = .g)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = linewidth_corporate_design) +
    geom_point(size = 1.4) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = report_years, labels = year_labels,
                       expand = c(.02, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) fmt(x, digits)) +
    scale_colour_corporate_design() +
    labs(caption = wrap_caption(source_caption), subtitle = subtitle) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = ncol)) +
    theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size,
                           axis.title = element_blank())
  if (zero) g <- g + geom_zeroline()
  g
}

# A chart of bars, one per category, read from top to bottom.
chart_ranked <- function(data, value, label, subtitle = "%", digits = 0,
                         wrap = 44, fill = NULL) {
  d <- data %>%
    mutate(.v = {{ value }}, .l = wrap_labels({{ label }}, wrap)) %>%
    arrange(.v) %>%
    mutate(.l = factor(.l, levels = .l))
  # `missing` and not `is.null`, because the argument is given as an
  # expression over the columns of the data and evaluating it here, outside
  # the data, is what `is.null` would do.
  g <- if (missing(fill)) {
    ggplot(d, aes(x = .v, y = .l)) +
      geom_col(fill = palette_corporate_design("cat")[1], width = 0.72)
  } else {
    d <- d %>% mutate(.f = {{ fill }})
    ggplot(d, aes(x = .v, y = .l, fill = .f)) +
      geom_col(width = 0.72) +
      scale_fill_corporate_design() +
      guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 3))
  }
  g +
    geom_zeroline(x = 0) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) fmt(x, digits),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .06))) +
    labs(caption = wrap_caption(source_caption), subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size, grid = "x",
                           axis.title = element_blank())
}
```

```{r cover, results='asis'}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The cover and the running head
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

ts <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x)) x <- "–"
  paste0("\"", typst_string(as.character(x)), "\"")
}

typst_kv <- function(items) {
  rows <- vapply(seq_along(items), function(i) {
    paste0("  text(size: 7.5pt, fill: soft, ", ts(names(items)[i]), "),\n",
           "  text(size: 8.5pt, ", ts(items[[i]]), "),")
  }, character(1))
  paste0("#grid(columns: (3.5cm, 1fr), row-gutter: 5.5pt, column-gutter: 6pt,\n",
         paste(rows, collapse = "\n"), "\n)")
}

n_findings <- sum(filing_state$findings)
n_errors <- sum(by_code$findings[by_code$severity == "error"])
n_warnings <- sum(by_code$findings[by_code$severity == "warning"])
n_infos <- sum(by_code$findings[by_code$severity == "info"])
share_clean <- mean(rated$clean) * 100
share_spotless <- mean(rated$spotless) * 100
share_identity <- mean(!identity_state$fails_identity) * 100

record_items <- list()
record_items[["Countries"]] <- paste(report_countries, collapse = ", ")
record_items[["Financial years"]] <- period_range
record_items[["Filings listed"]] <- fmt(n_listed)
record_items[["Of those, with facts"]] <- fmt(n_read)
record_items[["Checks run"]] <- fmt(n_checks)
record_items[["Checked on"]] <-
  if (checked_on[1] == checked_on[2]) format(checked_on[1], "%d %B %Y") else
    paste(format(checked_on[1], "%d %b %Y"), "–",
          format(checked_on[2], "%d %b %Y"))

found_items <- list()
found_items[["Findings"]] <- fmt(n_findings)
found_items[["Of those, errors"]] <- fmt(n_errors)
found_items[["Filings with an error"]] <-
  paste0(fmt(sum(rated$errors > 0)), " (", fmt(100 - share_clean, 1), " %)")

found_items[["Nothing found at all, %"]] <- fmt(share_spotless, 1)

## Contents

#outline(title: none, depth: 2, indent: 1em)

{{< pagebreak >}}

### How this report is built

```{r basis, results='asis'}
basis <- c(
  paste0("**What it reads.** Two Silver tables of the `esef` module of ",
         "fincommons: the table of filings, one row per filing listed in ",
         "the indexes of filings.xbrl.org, and the table of issues, one row ",
         "per record that failed a check. The table of issues is written by ",
         "`fincommons.esef.quality`, which runs the ", fmt(n_checks),
         " checks of the module over the facts and the filings and writes ",
         "what they found; this report does not re-run them. The catalogue ",
         "of checks in section 5 is read from the same file the module ",
         "reads, so what a code means here is what it means there."),
  paste0("**What a finding is.** A row of the table of issues: one record ",
         "that failed one check. Where the fault belongs to the report as a ",
         "whole -- a balance sheet that does not balance -- the record is ",
         "the filing, and there is one row. Where one figure is at fault -- ",
         "a fact with no value -- the record is the fact, and a filing has ",
         "as many rows as it has such facts. The two counts are therefore ",
         "different things, and this report names them apart throughout: ",
         "**findings** are rows, **filings** are the distinct filings those ",
         "rows name. No table adds one to the other."),
  paste0("**What it is counted against.** A check that reads the figures of ",
         "a report can only fire on a filing the table of facts holds facts ",
         "for. Of the ", fmt(n_listed), " filings listed in this selection, ",
         fmt(n_read), " carry facts. The share for each check in section 2 ",
         "is taken against whichever of the two populations the check is ",
         "asked of, and the population of each is in the table of checks ",
         "below; every other rate in this report -- the share free of ",
         "errors, the shares by year and by country, the bands of findings ",
         "per filing -- is taken over the ", fmt(n_read), " filings with ",
         "facts, which is the one population every check of the module was ",
         "asked about. A filing listed without facts is counted only in the ",
         "two checks that read the index. Over the whole index instead, a ",
         "record of which a part has been collected would read as sound ",
         "because nothing had looked at the rest of it."),
  paste0("**What a severity means.** An **error** is a finding that an ",
         "analysis cannot read past: the figures of the filing contradict ",
         "one another, or a period is impossible. A **warning** is a ",
         "finding that needs a human to look at the filing before its ",
         "figures are used. A **note** describes the filing without ",
         "faulting it. The three are this project's judgement of how much a ",
         "finding costs a reader, not a classification any regulator ",
         "publishes."),
  paste0("**What it does not do.** Nothing in the module corrects a figure ",
         "or drops a filing. A check writes a row and leaves the data as it ",
         "is, which is what lets the table of issues be read beside the ",
         "figures rather than instead of them. A filing with findings is ",
         "still in the table of facts, and whether to use it is the ",
         "reader's decision to make."))

cat(paste(basis, collapse = "\n\n"))
```

### The checks, and what each is asked of

  transmute(code = paste0("`", code, "`"),
            severity = severity_label(severity),
            title,
            population = recode(population,
                                listed = "Every filing",
                                read = "Filings with facts"))

knitr::kable(temp, align = "llll", col.names = c(
  "Code", "Severity", "What it finds", "Asked of"))
```

## 1 The record checked

### What was checked, by country

```{r record-country}
# One row per country: what the indexes list, how much of it carries facts,
# and whether the checks have run over it at all. A country with no row in
# the table of issues is either a country every check passed or one the
# checks were never asked about, and the two cannot be told apart from the
# tables.
temp <- filing_state %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY) %>%
  summarise(listed = n(),
            read = sum(read),
            issuers = n_distinct(LEI),
            checked = ifelse(COUNTRY[1] %in% checked_countries, "yes", "–"),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(listed), COUNTRY) %>%
  mutate(read_share = read / listed * 100)

knitr::kable(temp %>% transmute(COUNTRY, Issuers = fmt(issuers),
                                Listed = fmt(listed), Read = fmt(read),
                                `Read, %` = fmt(read_share, 1),
                                Checked = checked),
             align = "lrrrrl",
             col.names = c("Country", "Issuers", "Filings listed",
                           "With facts", "With facts, %", "Checks ran"))
```

```{r record-silence, results='asis'}
if (length(silent_countries) > 0) {
  cat("\nThe table of issues holds no row for ",
      paste(silent_countries, collapse = ", "),
      ". That is not a statement that those filings passed the checks: a ",
      "country the checks have not run over and a country in which every ",
      "check passed look the same in these two tables. Where such a country ",
      "has filings with facts, its filings are counted among the sound ones ",
      "in every rate below, and the record reads sounder than it has been ",
      "shown to be.\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("\nThe checks have run over every country of this selection, so a ",
      "filing with no finding is a filing every check passed.\n", sep = "")
}
```

## 2 What the checks found

### The findings, by severity

```{r found-severity, results='asis'}
n_rated_findings <- sum(rated$findings)

cat("The ", fmt(n_checks), " checks wrote ", fmt(n_findings),
    " findings over the ", fmt(n_listed), " filings listed: ", fmt(n_errors),
    " errors, ", fmt(n_warnings), " warnings and ", fmt(n_infos),
    " notes. Of those, ", fmt(n_rated_findings), " fall on the ",
    fmt(n_read), " filings with facts, which is the population every check ",
    "was asked of and the one the table and the shares below are taken ",
    "over; the remaining ", fmt(n_findings - n_rated_findings),
    " fall on filings the table of facts holds no fact for, where only the ",
    "two checks that read the index could fire at all. A filing can carry ",
    "findings of several severities, so the shares do not add to a ",
    "hundred.\n\n", sep = "")

if (nrow(orphans) > 0) {
  cat("\n", fmt(nrow(orphans)), " further rows of the table of issues name ",
      "filings the table of filings no longer lists, which is what a ",
      "withdrawn filing leaves behind. They are counted nowhere else in ",
      "this report.\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r severity-table}
# Both counts over the filings with facts, which is what keeps a row of
# this table from putting findings of one population beside filings of
# another.
temp <- rated %>%
  summarise(across(c(errors, warnings, infos), ~ sum(.x > 0)),
            none = sum(spotless)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "severity", values_to = "filings") %>%
  mutate(label = recode(severity, errors = "An error",
                        warnings = "A warning", infos = "A note",
                        none = "Nothing at all"),
         findings = c(sum(rated$errors), sum(rated$warnings),
                      sum(rated$infos), 0),
         share = filings / n_read * 100)

knitr::kable(temp %>% transmute(label, Findings = fmt(findings),
                                Filings = fmt(filings),
                                Share = fmt(share, 1)),
             align = "lrrr",
             col.names = c("Filings carrying", "Findings",
                           "Filings with facts", "Of those, %"))
```

### How the findings fall across the record

```{r found-concentration}
# A record in which every filing carries one finding and one in which a
# tenth of the filings carry ten are the same count and are not the same
# problem. These are the bands of findings per filing.
bands <- c(0, 1, 2, 3, 6, 11, Inf)
band_labels <- c("None", "1", "2", "3 – 5", "6 – 10", "> 10")

temp <- rated %>%
  mutate(band = cut(findings, breaks = bands, labels = band_labels,
                    include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE)) %>%
  count(fy, band, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  group_by(fy) %>%
  mutate(share = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(label = band)

render_years(temp, share, digits = 1,
             header = "Findings per filing with facts, %",
             order = band_labels)
```

```{r found-concentration-note, results='asis'}
top_share <- rated %>%
  arrange(desc(findings)) %>%
  slice_head(n = max(1, round(nrow(rated) / 100)))
cat("\nThe loudest one per cent of the filings with facts -- ",
    fmt(nrow(top_share)), " of them -- carry ",
    fmt(sum(top_share$findings) / max(n_findings, 1) * 100, 1),
    " % of all findings. A count of findings is therefore not a measure of ",
    "how much of the record is usable; the share of filings free of errors ",
    "in section 3 is.\n", sep = "")
```

```{r clean-note, results='asis'}
cat("No error was found in ", fmt(sum(rated$clean)), " of the ",
    fmt(n_read), " filings with facts, and nothing at all in ",
    fmt(sum(rated$spotless)), ". ",
    "The first is the share an analysis that reads figures out of these ",
    "filings can work with; the second is the share about which nothing at ",
    "all was found, which is a stricter test than most uses need -- a note ",
    "that a report tags most of its figures under its own concepts is a ",
    "fact about the report and not a fault in it.\n", sep = "")
```

### The five identities

```{r identities, results='asis'}
cat("Five of the checks test a report against itself: that the balance ",
    "sheet balances, that the two halves of the asset side add to the ",
    "total, that revenue less the cost of sales is the gross profit, that ",
    "the result before tax less the tax is the result, and that the three ",
    "cash flows sum to the movement in cash. They are the checks an ",
    "analysis that reads a statement out of a filing rests on, and they are ",
    "read together here because a filing that fails any one of them cannot ",
    "be read as a set of statements.\n\n", sep = "")

cat("All five hold in ", fmt(sum(!identity_state$fails_identity)),
    " of the ", fmt(n_read), " filings with facts, ",
    fmt(share_identity, 1), " % of them.\n", sep = "")
```

```{r identities-table}
temp <- by_code %>%
  filter(ISSUE %in% identity_codes) %>%
  transmute(title,
            Filings = fmt(affected),
            Share = fmt(share, 1))

knitr::kable(temp, align = "lrr",
             col.names = c("The identity", "Filings failing it",
                           "Of the filings with facts, %"))
```

```{r identities-silent, results='asis'}
# An identity can only be tested where the filing tags both sides of it. A
# filing that tags neither passes by silence, which is a different thing
# from passing, and the MISS_ checks are what makes that visible.
miss <- by_code %>% filter(grepl("^MISS_", ISSUE), ISSUE != "MISS_FACT_VALUE")
cat("\nAn identity is only tested where the filing tags the lines it rests ",
    "on. A filing that tags neither side of one passes it by silence, which ",
    "is not the same as passing it: ",
    paste(sprintf("%s in %s %% of the filings with facts",
                  tolower(miss$title), fmt(miss$share, 1)),
          collapse = "; "),
    ". Those are the ", nrow(miss), " `MISS_` checks, and they are what ",
    "keeps a silent pass from reading as a sound report.\n", sep = "")
```

### What the repository's own validation found

```{r repo-validation, results='asis'}
# The repository validates every filing it takes in. Its counts are not this
# report's checks and are not re-run here; one of the checks carries them
# into the table of issues so that they sit beside the rest.
temp <- filings %>%
  summarise(with_errors = sum(ERRORS > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            with_warnings = sum(WARNINGS > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            with_inconsistencies = sum(INCONSISTENCIES > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            errors = sum(ERRORS, na.rm = TRUE))

cat("filings.xbrl.org validates every filing it takes in and records what ",
    "its rules found. Those counts are the repository's, not this ",
    "report's: the `VALIDATION_ERRORS` check carries them into the table of ",
    "issues so that they sit beside the rest, and nothing here re-ran a ",
    "rule. Of the ", fmt(n_listed), " filings checked, ",
    fmt(temp$with_errors), " carry at least one validation error, ",
    fmt(temp$with_warnings), " at least one warning and ",
    fmt(temp$with_inconsistencies),
    " at least one calculation inconsistency. A validation error does not ",
    "mean a figure is wrong -- it means the filing does not meet the ",
    "format -- and the repository publishes the filing either way.\n",
    sep = "")
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

## 4 What this report cannot say

```{r limits, results='asis'}
limits <- c(
  paste("**Whether a finding is a fault.** A check names a record that did",
        "not hold to a rule of this project. Several of the rules are held",
        "to by sound filings only most of the time: an issuer presenting",
        "assets in order of liquidity has no current and non-current",
        "subtotals to add up, one presenting expenses by nature has no cost",
        "of sales, and a bank's revenue is interest income tagged",
        "elsewhere. The catalogue in section 5 says for each check what a",
        "legitimate cause looks like, and no count in this report has one",
        "subtracted from it."),
  paste("**Whether a silence is a pass.** A check tests what a filing",
        "tagged. A filing that tagged neither side of an identity is not",
        "named by the identity check, and a filing the repository published",
        "no facts for is not named by any check that reads a figure. Both",
        "are counted here as filings with no finding of that check, which",
        "is why the `MISS_` checks and the `NO_FACTS` note are in the same",
        "table as the identities: they are the record of where the other",
        "checks had nothing to look at."),
  paste("**Whether the checks have run.** The table of issues holds the",
        "rows of the partitions the checks were last asked about. A country",
        "or a year the checks have not run over has no rows and is counted",
        "here as a part of the record with no findings. Section 1 names the",
        "countries this applies to; a report whose first table shows a",
        "country with no run cannot be read as a report on that country."),
  paste("**Whether a figure is right.** Nothing in the module reads a",
        "report. An identity that holds says the figures a filing tagged",
        "are consistent with one another, not that they are the figures the",
        "accounts show, and a filing can tag a wrong number consistently",
        "in every statement. Only the filing itself, which the repository",
        "publishes in its viewer, settles that."),
  paste("**What the severities are worth.** The three severities are this",
        "project's judgement of what a finding costs a reader of the data.",
        "They are not a classification ESMA publishes, they are not the",
        "repository's, and an analysis with different needs should read the",
        "codes rather than the severities: a note that most of a report is",
        "tagged under the issuer's own concepts stops a cross-sectional",
        "comparison dead, and an error in a cash flow identity does not",
        "touch a reader who only wants the balance sheet."),
  paste("**What happens next.** The module writes findings and changes",
        "nothing. No figure in the table of facts is corrected, no filing",
        "is set aside, and a filing that fails every check is read by the",
        "rest of the module exactly as one that passes. A pipeline that",
        "wants to act on a finding has to do so itself, which is what the",
        "table of issues is for."))

cat(paste(limits, collapse = "\n\n"))
```

## 5 The checks in full

```{r catalogue-intro, results='asis'}
cat("The catalogue the module ships, read from the same file the checks ",
    "read it from. Each entry says what the check finds, what a finding ",
    "means and what to do about it. The order is by severity.\n", sep = "")
```

```{r catalogue-full, results='asis'}
for (level in severities) {
  rows <- catalogue %>% filter(severity == level)
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) next
  heading <- switch(level,
                    error = "Errors",
                    warning = "Warnings",
                    info = "Notes")
  cat("\n### ", heading, "\n\n", sep = "")
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(rows))) {
    found <- by_code %>% filter(ISSUE == rows$code[i])
    cat("**`", rows$code[i], "` — ", rows$title[i], ".** ",
        rows$meaning[i], " ",
        "*Found in ", fmt(found$affected), " of the ",
        fmt(found$denominator), " filings it is asked of",
        if (found$affected > 0)
          paste0(", ", fmt(found$findings), " findings") else "",
        ".* ",
        "*What to do:* ", rows$remedy[i], "\n\n", sep = "")
  }
}
```

              paste(format(checked_on[1], "%d %b %Y"), "–",
                    format(checked_on[2], "%d %b %Y")),
            format(Sys.Date(), "%d %B %Y")))

knitr::kable(temp, col.names = c("", ""), align = "lr")
```

### How to run the checks again

```{r rerun, results='asis'}
cat("The table of issues is rebuilt a partition at a time, and a partition ",
    "is rewritten as a whole when it is checked again, so a finding that ",
    "was fixed in the data leaves no row behind. From Python:\n\n",
    "```python\n",
    "from pyspark.sql import SparkSession\n",
    "from fincommons.esef.quality import update_silver_esef_quality\n\n",
    "spark = SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate()\n",
    "update_silver_esef_quality(spark, \"paths.yaml\", countries=[\"AT\"])\n",
    "```\n\n",
    "`fincommons.dataquality.describe_check` turns a code into the ",
    "sentences printed in section 5, `issue_counts` counts the table by ",
    "code, and `with_issues` and `suppressed` join the findings onto the ",
    "figures so that a pipeline can act on them.\n", sep = "")
```

### Sources

```{r sources, results='asis'}
sources <- c(
  paste("**The filings and the reports.** filings.xbrl.org, run by XBRL",
        "International, which collects the reports filed with the officially",
        "appointed mechanism of each member state, validates them and",
        "publishes for each filing the report package as filed, the report",
        "as xBRL-JSON where it could convert it, and the counts of what its",
        "validation found. The `esef` module reads its yearly indexes and",
        "the xBRL-JSON."),
  paste("**The checks.** `fincommons.esef.quality`, with the machinery",
        "common to the regimes in `fincommons.dataquality` and the",
        "descriptions in `fincommons/data/dataquality_checks.csv`. All three",
        "are part of the open-source project fincommons and are the only",
        "source of the rules counted here."),
  paste("**The taxonomy.** The IFRS taxonomy and ESMA's additions to it name",
        "the concepts the checks look for. A concept an issuer created for",
        "its own report is not one the checks can read, which is what the",
        "`MISS_` checks and the note on extension-heavy reports record."))

cat(paste(sources, collapse = "\n\n"))
```
